subject.title: fix(llm): summarize ephemeral tool results to preserve prefix cache

question: Which tool-result visibility policy should OpenClaw use for the DeepSeek prefix-cache regression: narrow placeholders for heartbeat/status-style outputs, existing truncation/isolation controls, or a broader provider-payload policy?
rationale: The right fix changes model-visible session semantics and provider payload bytes; code inspection can show this PR is too broad, but maintainers need to choose the durable behavior boundary for heartbeat/status versus information-bearing tools.

options.title: Narrow to status-style outputs
options.body: Rebase onto `packages/ai`, keep only low-information heartbeat/status outputs behind the placeholder policy, and require focused tests plus live DeepSeek cache proof.

options.title: Use truncation and isolation instead
options.body: Close or replace the placeholder approach and continue with bounded truncation, context pruning, or heartbeat isolated-session defaults for the cache/cost issue.

options.title: Accept a broader payload policy
options.body: Maintainers can deliberately hide more tool outputs only with explicit tool-by-tool semantics, user-visible risk acceptance, and live provider proof.

recommendation.title: Narrow to status-style outputs
recommendation.body: Rebase onto `packages/ai`, keep only low-information heartbeat/status outputs behind the placeholder policy, and require focused tests plus live DeepSeek cache proof.

likelyOwner.reason: Vincent has the strongest current-main signal on provider conversion and tool-call payload behavior touched by this PR.
